citation.authors: Niu Y, Yang Y, Zhang Z-Q, Li Z-M, Sun H
citation.title: Floral closure induced by pollination in gynodioecious Cyananthus delavayi (Campanulaceae): effects of pollen load and type, floral morph and fitness consequences
citation.locations: Study site 27°54'N 99°38'E, 3355 m, Shangri-la, Yunnan, southwestern China
source_locations: Methods sections pollen load and fitness, pp.1259–1260
Results flower closure and pollen-load response
citation.acquisition: Open-access original full text via PMC; group n inferred strictly from original Table 1 parentheses, not raw flower observations

female_experiment.table_basis: Female flowers with both closure observation and female-fitness result available
female_experiment.source_note: With 20 grains, 63.5% of analyzed female flowers closed; initial design randomized 72 flowers per dose but not all fruits were retained, so original result pertains to analyzed subset
female_experiment.randomization_unit: Flowers nested within 24 plants; exact maternal clustering not recoverable from published table

perfect_experiment.ten_grain_condition: Zero recorded closure of perfect flowers with 10-grain exposure, but most fruits were lost and their female fitness was not usable
perfect_experiment.source_note: Table 1 records 49 cross and 49 self only at 20 and 30 grains; do not treat missing 10-grain perfect fruit data as zero seed

closure_latency.sample_type: Separate hand-crossed flowers of female and perfect plants; latency distributions were not reconstructed

paired_prevent_closure_sufficient_cross_.methods: Two flowers per source plant, one constrained open with fine wire ring, all hand pollinated with sufficient cross-pollen
paired_prevent_closure_sufficient_cross_.interpretation: Neither test detected additional seed benefit of preventing closure under sufficient pollination; these tests are not closure-prevention effects under pollen limitation

observed_interpretation.female_closed_at_20_grains: 63.5% among 63 analyzed flowers, not 72 initially exposed
observed_interpretation.female_cross_self_comparison: Sex and pollen type contrasts distinct; the non-significant self vs cross closure response in perfect flowers is not equivalence
observed_interpretation.male_phase_bottleneck_other_sources: 2015/2021 controlled pollen removal delays the start of the female phase in hermaphrodites; not same cohort
observed_interpretation.female_phase_bottleneck_this_source: 2011 premature closure can remove future pollen-receipt opportunities after very low pollen deposition
observed_interpretation.true_fitness_scope: Maternal seeds and ovule/fertilization indices; no direct male paternity, lifetime fitness, genetic divergence or SLK origin gate
observed_interpretation.author_donor_manipulation_inference: The original discussion explicitly says this work does not sufficiently verify sexual conflict or pollen-donor manipulation

claim_limits: Counts from published Table 1 used to exactly reconstruct Pearson chi-square for the female usable subset, but raw individual-level data and maternal clustering are unavailable
216 treated female flowers but 163 usable; 180 treated perfect flowers but 98 usable; unequal missing outcomes may bias percentages
The original tests use SPSS/JMP treating analyzed flowers as units; reconstructing chi-square does not correct potential within-plant dependence
Different original articles in 2011, 2015, 2017 and 2021 share species/research programs, not a single cohort or four independent evolutionary transitions
A closure correlation with low fruit production in field flowers does not prove causal female-fitness loss from the closure itself
Ring manipulation under sufficient pollen showed no statistically detectable seed response; this does not estimate benefits of keeping flowers open under insufficient pollen
2011 authors themselves explicitly say sexual conflict or pollen-donor manipulation are not established by this experiment
2021 Dryad 10.5061/dryad.hmgqnk9f7 is listed by PubMed but the landing and file content were not retrieved here; no claim of original 2021 raw-data reanalysis
No SLK L, Phi, g0, Delta_R, historical origin, allelic invasion or fixation estimates from this source
The female versus perfect flower 20-grain comparison is standardized for cross-pollen dose but not a randomized within-genotype sex-architecture intervention.

cross_morph_comparison_at_20_grains.denominator_warning: Same pollen-dose condition, different floral morphs and source plants; sex morph was not a randomized treatment
cross_morph_comparison_at_20_grains.question: Does differentiated female morph have the same pollen-triggered shutdown sensitivity as perfect flowers? Original test detects a difference.
